title: Memorable Meetings & Story Time
subtitle: Build vocabulary for chance encounters and preview two useful past tenses.

sections.label: Lesson Notes
sections.title: What we explored
sections.intro: We listened to stories about memorable meetings and chance encounters. Complete the writing task from the previous lesson and send your teacher a screenshot when it is ready.

cards.title: Story order
cards.text: Use first, then, afterwards, eventually and finally to make a story easy to follow.

cards.title: A quick preview
cards.text: Use past simple for a finished event. Use past continuous for an action that was in progress when another event happened. We will study this in more detail next lesson.

cards.title: Chance encounters
cards.text: Run into means meet someone unexpectedly.

sections.label: Grammar
sections.title: A first look: past simple and past continuous

patterns.label: Finished event
patterns.explanation: Past simple tells us about a completed event.

patterns.label: Action in progress
patterns.explanation: Past continuous shows an action in progress at that time.

patterns.label: Two actions together
patterns.explanation: The longer action can be in progress when a shorter event happens.

questions.q: I ___ for the bus when I saw my neighbour.
questions.explanation: Was waiting shows the action already in progress when the neighbour appeared.

questions.q: While we ___ home, it started to rain.
questions.explanation: Were walking shows the ongoing action at that moment.

questions.q: She ___ her old teacher at the station yesterday.
questions.explanation: Saw is past simple for one finished meeting yesterday.

questions.q: Choose the natural story sentence.
opt: I was run into my cousin.
I ran into while I wait.
I was waiting when I was saw him.
I was waiting when I ran into my cousin.
questions.explanation: Was waiting gives the background action; ran into is the completed event.

cards.meaning: find something for the first time

cards.meaning: one of two siblings who look exactly the same

cards.title: confused

cards.title: eventually
cards.meaning: in the end, after some time

cards.title: a few weeks later
cards.meaning: some weeks after an earlier event
cards.example: A few weeks later, they met again.

activities.prompt: Write a short story about a memorable or chance meeting. Use first, then, afterwards, eventually or finally. Include one past simple sentence and one past continuous sentence.
activities.guidance: Aim for about 100 words. When you finish, take a screenshot and send it to your teacher for review.

readings.title: A strange meeting
readings.text: A few weeks ago, Leyla was waiting for a bus after work. While she was looking at her phone, she heard someone say her name. She looked up and saw an identical twin of a friend from school. At first, Leyla was confused because she did not know her friend had a twin. They talked for ten minutes, and afterwards Leyla caught the next bus. Eventually, she sent her friend a message about the strange experience.

opt: She did not know about the twin
